title: Klieg Light
subtitle: Opening Night at the Pantheon, a Rifle in the Glare, What Goes Into the Microphone

setting.name: Hollywood, Wednesday 1 to Saturday 4 October 1947
setting.description: Three days of offers and one night of light. Everyone now knows the party has the green ledger, the negatives, or both, and everyone comes to buy it: Bernard Castellane, head of the studio, in his office over the main gate; Wendell Haig, through a lawyer with a cheque; Lyle Preston of the committee, with a promise; Harlan Shay, with a confession he cannot quite make. Emory Thorne is still in town, still under contract, and he has taken a job with the searchlight company that will light The Gilded Hour's premiere. On Saturday night the Pantheon Theatre on Hollywood Boulevard opens its doors under six searchlights and a battery of klieg lights, with bleachers of fans, a radio microphone on the forecourt, every newspaper in town, two councilmen, the studio, the committee, and Vivian Lark in a silver gown, carrying a green ledger in her evening bag.
setting.atmosphere: Glare. The premiere is the brightest place in Los Angeles: searchlight beams standing up into the sky like the columns of a temple, klieg lights on the marquee so hot the air shimmers, flashbulbs going off in volleys, the crowd behind the ropes roaring each name. Outside the light everything is black. Nobody standing in the forecourt can see the roof, and nobody on the roof can be looked at. That is Thorne's plan and the scenario's image. Before the night, the tone is quieter and harder: men in good offices explaining calmly why the truth would be a catastrophe, and some of them being right. The ending is a choice, not a fight. Give it room.

keyLocations.name: The Pantheon Theatre, Hollywood Boulevard
keyLocations.description: A movie palace built in 1926 in the style of a Greek temple that has been to Egypt on holiday: a forecourt sixty feet deep with a fountain, a colonnade, a marquee two storeys high, a lobby of gilt and red plush, an auditorium for two thousand under a ceiling of painted stars, a projection booth above the balcony with two carbon-arc projectors, and a flat roof over the marquee where the klieg lights are mounted. Across the boulevard, on a vacant lot, the searchlight trucks: six army-surplus sixty-inch searchlights on trailers.
features: The forecourt: the red carpet, the ropes, the bleachers for fans, the radio booth and its microphone on a stand by the fountain

The marquee roof: a battery of klieg lights and two spotlights on swivel mounts, each run by an operator, reached by an iron ladder from the projection-booth corridor; looking toward it from the forecourt is looking into the sun
The projection booth: two projectors, a rewind bench, the nitrate print of The Gilded Hour in eight reels, a fire shutter
The lobby, the stage door alley, the manager's office and the fire stairs
The searchlight lot across the boulevard: six trucks, generators, cables, and a crew of twelve
encounters: Five thousand fans, two hundred guests, forty photographers, twelve LAPD officers on crowd duty under Lt. Dolan, and the KHLW radio announcer, Chick Lorimer
Emory Thorne on the marquee roof as spotlight operator No. 2, with a hunting rifle in the spotlight's case
Lt. Dolan and two Crooked Cops with instructions (from Haig, through Shay or directly) to arrest Vivian 'for theft of club property' before she reaches the microphone
Lyle Preston and two Federal Agents, with a federal warrant for 'documents relevant to the committee's inquiry', meaning the ledger
secrets: At 8:40 p.m., by the run-of-show, Chick Lorimer calls Vivian Lark to the microphone and spotlight No. 2 holds on her for thirty seconds while she speaks. Thorne will fire on the twentieth second. Anyone on the forecourt trying to look up at the roof during the cue is blinded (Constitution save DC 13 or blinded until the end of their next turn).

On the roof, the klieg lights are carbon arcs: anyone shoved into one takes 2d6 fire damage; anyone looking into one at close range is blinded as above; a shot into a lamp housing makes it explode in a shower of glass and sparks (1d6 fire, 10-foot radius, DEX save DC 12 for half) and goes dark.

Thorne's escape is planned: down the iron ladder, along the projection corridor, out of the fire door to the alley, into a rented Ford with the engine running, driven by a Getaway Driver. He leaves the rifle.

keyLocations.name: Bernard Castellane's Office, the Castellane Lot
keyLocations.description: Over the Moorish gate, reached by a private elevator: walnut panelling, a desk the size of a car, a bust of Castellane by a sculptor who flattered him, and a window over the lot from which he can see every stage. Bernard Castellane, sixty-four, came from nothing in 1921 and is about to go back to it.
features: The desk, the bust, and a framed telegram from 1927 congratulating the studio on its first talkie
A side door into the boardroom, where the studio's bankers met on Monday
encounters: Bernard Castellane, who summons the party on Wednesday, offers $25,000 for the ledger and the negatives, and explains, with real tears, about the six hundred people who work for him
secrets: CLUE P3a (core, if the party listens and asks): Castellane has promised Lyle Preston that the studio will give the committee 'full cooperation', meaning names, including Abel Kurland's, which costs nothing now that he is dead, and a dozen living writers, a designer, two actors and a grip. The list is in his desk drawer. He calls it 'the price of staying open'.

Castellane does not know Shay was at the pool. He does not know about Mabry. He knows about the money and the councilmen and Encino Verde, and he thinks that is ordinary business, which in his world it is.

keyLocations.name: Starlite Searchlight Service, Burbank
keyLocations.description: A yard of army-surplus searchlight trucks and generators by the railroad tracks in Burbank, an office in a Quonset hut, and Mr. Hap Dorsey, the owner, who rents light to every premiere, car dealership and supermarket opening in Los Angeles.
features: The work board and the crew manifest for Saturday's job at the Pantheon
The equipment store: spotlight cases, carbons, cables
encounters: Hap Dorsey, a talkative veteran who ran searchlights in an anti-aircraft battalion and will tell you about it
secrets: CLUE P1a (core, asking Dorsey about Saturday's crew): 'Four men on the roof is what the job needs. Five on the manifest. Studio called Tuesday, a Mr. Haig's office, said a fella named Thomas was a good operator and needed the work, they'd pay his wage. Quiet fella. Knows his carbons. Asked to run number two, the follow spot on the microphone.' Dorsey has a manifest with 'E. Thomas, No. 2 spot (roof)'.

keyLocations.name: The Hotel Cordova, Hollywood Boulevard
keyLocations.description: A twelve-storey hotel with a Spanish lobby, a palm court, a bar where agents sign people, and rooms over the boulevard. Lyle Preston has a suite on the eighth floor. Emory Thorne, as E. Thomas, has room 1104, with a view of the Pantheon's roof six blocks east.
features: Room 1104: a single bed, a suitcase, a long case that says KLIEG CARBONS on it, and a window over Hollywood Boulevard
Preston's suite 812: files, a typewriter, a stenographer, and a briefcase that never leaves him
The desk clerk, who can be persuaded ($5) that the party are E. Thomas's colleagues
encounters: Emory Thorne, if the party goes in while he is in (he is out from noon to six on Thursday and Friday, rehearsing with the searchlight crew)
Lyle Preston, who notices the party in the lobby and invites them up
secrets: CLUE P1b (core, searching room 1104): a union card of the motion-picture projectionists and lamp operators in the name Edward Thomas; a typed note, 'No. 2 spot, roof. 8:40 cue, hold 30'; a box of .30-06 cartridges with five missing; a fine jeweller's saw in a felt roll, the kind used on brake lines; and a Pacific Electric timetable with the Valley line circled. The long case is empty: the rifle is already on the Pantheon roof, inside the No. 2 spotlight's case.

CLUE P3b (core, Preston's suite or briefcase): a typed list on Castellane Pictures letterhead, 'persons who may be of interest to the committee', with Abel Kurland's name at the top, and fourteen others. If any player character has a past the committee would like (Roz's union card, Percy's clients), their name is on it in pencil, added this week.

keyLocations.name: Harlan Shay's House, Los Feliz Hills
keyLocations.description: A white Regency house with a view of the whole city, books he has read, records he plays, and a wife who died in 1940 in every photograph. He has been sleeping in a chair.
features: The study, the green Packard in the garage with a new right front fender, and a ledger of the studio's special-services account he keeps at home because he trusts nobody
encounters: Harlan Shay, who knows the party knows
secrets: CLUE P2a (core, Shay's special-services ledger): six years of payments to 'F.D.' ($300 a month, and $1,000 on 24 September 1947) and one to 'W.N., $200, 24 Sept.'. With Walter Ness's statement and Dolan's 6:50 phone-in, the DA has a case against Dolan and the coroner's office.
If the party has three K2 clues and confronts him, Shay tells the whole truth about the pool, including the three minutes. See the dmTips for what he will do next.

Shay will tell the party something they need, if they ask: Haig called him on Tuesday to arrange for Thomas, 'the man from the airport in August', to join the searchlight crew. Shay arranged it, and only then, at last, let himself understand what Thomas is for. (Clue P1c, alternate route.)

keyLocations.name: The Studio Publicity Office and the Run-of-Show
keyLocations.description: The publicity department in a two-storey building by the commissary, full of press agents, photographs, mimeograph machines and cigarette smoke. On Thursday it is producing the premiere's run-of-show: a minute-by-minute schedule of arrivals, cues for the radio, and lighting cues.
features: The mimeographed run-of-show and its lighting cue sheet, three pages, stapled
encounters: Agnes Whitlow (companion), who supervises the premiere's continuity because nobody else can, and Mr. Jerry Fine, head of publicity, who is very happy Vivian is back
secrets: CLUE P1c (core, Agnes or anyone reading the cue sheet): '8:40. LORIMER calls MISS LARK to microphone. No. 2 SPOT (roof) picks up and HOLDS 30 sec. All other lights down to half.' Pencilled in the margin in an unfamiliar hand that Agnes has never seen: 'confirm 20'. The No. 2 operator asked Jerry Fine on Thursday to confirm the cue would hold at least twenty seconds.

synopsis: Everyone wants what the party has. Bernard Castellane offers $25,000 and an honest account of how many people will lose their jobs if the ledger is published, and admits he has promised the committee names to save his studio, Abel Kurland's among them. Wendell Haig offers $40,000 through a lawyer and a veiled threat. Lyle Preston of the committee offers immunity, and a federal warrant if immunity does not appeal. Harlan Shay, confronted with what the party knows, tells them the truth about the three minutes at the edge of the pool and asks what he should do. Meanwhile Emory Thorne has joined the crew that will light The Gilded Hour's premiere, as operator of the follow spot that will hold on Vivian Lark at the radio microphone at 8:40 on Saturday night; a searchlight company's manifest, Thorne's hotel room and the premiere's cue sheet give the plan away. On opening night the Pantheon's forecourt is the brightest place in Los Angeles. Dolan's men try to arrest Vivian before she can reach the microphone, Preston's federal agents try to seize the ledger, and on the marquee roof, in the blinding glare of the klieg lights, the party must stop a professional before the twentieth second. Then Vivian is at the microphone with a live radio audience, the whole city in dinner jackets in front of her, and the green ledger in her hand, and the party decides, with her or against her, what goes into the microphone, and what becomes of Harlan Shay.
hook: Thursday morning's papers have it on page one, with the portrait Shay showed the party ten days ago: VIVIAN LARK HOME FROM DESERT REST. STAR TO ATTEND GILDED HOUR PREMIERE SATURDAY. 'I've never felt better,' says the actress. 'I'm looking forward to saying a few words.' On page three, below the fold: COUNCIL TO VOTE ON VALLEY WATER TUESDAY. On page five: CLUB OWNER FOUND SHOT AT MOVIE RANCH, or, if the party saved him, SIROCCO OWNER LEAVES TOWN. And in the morning mail, at whatever address the party has been using, a cream envelope with the Castellane castle on it and a note in a large old man's hand: 'I should like to meet you. My office, eleven o'clock. You have something of mine, and I have something you should know. B. Castellane.'

conclusions.conclusion: Emory Thorne will shoot Vivian at 8:40 on Saturday from the No. 2 spotlight on the Pantheon's marquee roof, hidden by the glare.
clues: P1a: Starlite Searchlight's fifth man, E. Thomas, recommended by Haig's office, who asked for the No. 2 spot (Burbank)
P1b: Room 1104 at the Hotel Cordova: the union card, the cue note, the cartridges, the saw, the empty rifle case (Hollywood Boulevard)
P1c: The run-of-show cue sheet, 'No. 2 spot holds 30 sec', with 'confirm 20' pencilled in; or Shay's admission that Haig asked him to place Thomas on the crew (studio publicity, Shay's house)

conclusions.conclusion: Harlan Shay paid Lt. Dolan and Deputy Coroner Ness to bury Kurland's death; the DA can prove it.
clues: P2a: Shay's special-services ledger: 'F.D.' monthly and $1,000 on 24 September; 'W.N.' $200 (Shay's house)
P2b: Walter Ness's statement about the pre-typed report and the envelope (from kl-scenario-002)
P2c: The Hollywood Division desk log, Dolan's 6:50 phone-in (from kl-scenario-002)
P2d (bonus): Dolan's Arrowhead cabin deed, bought for cash in 1944 (Hall of Records, Research DC 12)

conclusions.conclusion: Bernard Castellane has promised the committee names to save the studio, Kurland's first among them, and the price of exposing the ledger includes what the committee does with the scandal.
clues: P3a: Castellane's own admission and the list in his desk (Castellane's office)
P3b: The list on studio letterhead in Preston's briefcase, with player characters' names added in pencil (Hotel Cordova)
P3c: Percy Ainsworth's or Roz Keane's sources: three of Percy's clients and two Courier reporters have been called by Preston this week, each asked about 'a Castellane list'

acts.title: Act 1: Offers
acts.description: Wednesday 1 to Friday 3 October. The powerful come to buy. Each offer is honest about something. Use this act to lay out the choice the party will make on Saturday, and to let them find Thorne's plan. The confrontation with Shay belongs here if it has not happened.
objectives: Hear Castellane's offer and what it costs
Hear Haig's offer and his threat
Deal with Lyle Preston and his warrant
Confront Harlan Shay, and decide what to do with him
Make a plan for the premiere with Vivian

scenes.name: Six Hundred People
scenes.description: Bernard Castellane's office, Thursday at eleven. He is old, tired, intelligent and absolutely sincere. He offers $25,000 for the ledger and the negatives. He explains: if this comes out, the bankers close the studio by Christmas; six hundred people, carpenters, wardrobe women, electricians, Agnes Whitlow, Bunny Shearer, Ken Hirano, lose their jobs; and the committee, handed a scandal, will call Castellane Pictures a nest of Reds and blacklist everyone who ever worked there. He admits he has promised Preston names. He does not think he had a choice. He might be right.
scenes.readAloud: Bernard Castellane is smaller than his portrait in the lobby and older than his bust, a stooped man in a perfect suit with a cigar he does not light and the eyes of someone who has not slept. He does not get up. 'In 1921 I had a camera, a horse and a cousin who could fall off it,' he says. 'Now I have six hundred people and a bank that will close me on the first of January unless the Valley comes through. You have my death warrant in your pocket, I think. Sit down. I'd like to tell you what it will cost, and then I'd like to tell you what I'll pay.'

skillChecks.success: Everything he says about the studio's money and the six hundred jobs is true. He did not know about Mabry or the pool, and the news, if you give it, ages him ten years. The list of names he is less sorry about than he says.
skillChecks.failure: He is a mogul. Moguls cry when it is useful. You cannot tell whether this is.

skillChecks.success: Castellane agrees to tear up the list and refuse the committee, whatever the party does with the ledger. It will cost him dearly in Washington. He does it because you made him ashamed. (This opens a better version of every ending.)
skillChecks.failure: 'I'm too old to be brave,' he says, 'and too poor.'

scenes.name: The Pool, Again
scenes.description: Harlan Shay, at his house in the hills or in his bungalow. If the party has the K2 clues, he tells the truth, including the three minutes. Then he asks what he should do. His options, which he will name himself if the party does not: turn himself in to the District Attorney (and testify against Dolan, Ness, Haig and the councilmen); run to Mexico (he has a car and $5,000); 'make it right' at the premiere; or take the coward's way out, which the party can prevent. He will do what the party advises if they advise it honestly.
scenes.readAloud: 'He swung at me,' Shay says. 'Abel couldn't hit a barn. I hit him back. I hadn't hit anyone since 1918. He went backwards and his head hit the edge and he went in, and he was moving, he was trying, and I stood there.' He looks at his bandaged hand. 'I could have reached him. I was thinking about the photograph. Me and Fenwick and the envelope. I was thinking that if he came up, the studio was finished, and I was finished, and I stood there and I thought about it until he stopped. It was a long time. It was a very long time.' He looks up at you. 'So. You're the detectives. What do I do now?'

skillChecks.success: Every word is true. He has not said it out loud before and he will never be able to unsay it.
skillChecks.failure: He might be performing. He has worked with actors for twenty years.

skillChecks.success: Shay agrees to whatever the party asks of him that is not cruel: to go to the DA on Monday, to testify, to help at the premiere. He tells you Haig asked him to put 'Thomas' on the searchlight crew (P1c).
skillChecks.failure: Shay agrees to wait until after the premiere. He does not promise what he will do after that.

scenes.name: Number Two Spot
scenes.description: Finding Thorne's plan: Starlite Searchlight in Burbank, room 1104 at the Cordova, the cue sheet in the publicity office. Any two of the three make it plain; all three make it certain. Thorne is out rehearsing from noon to six on Thursday and Friday; room 1104 can be searched then. If the party is seen (Heat 6 or more, or a failed check), Thorne knows they know, and changes position: the rifle moves to the searchlight lot across the boulevard, on the platform of searchlight truck No. 4, which makes the shot longer and the escape easier.
scenes.readAloud: The Quonset hut smells of carbon dust and coffee and hot metal. Hap Dorsey talks with his hands about the Battle of the Bulge and the searchlights they bounced off the clouds to make artificial moonlight, and then he finds the manifest for Saturday under a doughnut box and runs a grease-stained finger down it. 'Four on the roof, two on each truck,' he says. 'And this fella. Thomas. Number two spot.' He scratches his head. 'Didn't need five. Studio's paying, though.'

skillChecks.success: In and out of room 1104 without the clerk or the house detective seeing (P1b).
skillChecks.failure: The house detective (Rival Private Eye, working for the hotel) catches you in the corridor. Talk your way out (Deception DC 14), pay him $20, or fight; either way, he mentions it to E. Thomas, who now knows (see above).

skillChecks.success: In room 1104, the jeweller's saw in its felt roll matches the cut on Mabry's brake line, if anyone saw it in kl-scenario-003. This is the M3 conclusion confirmed beyond doubt.
skillChecks.failure: You find the core clues and miss the saw's significance until later.

scenes.name: Mr. Preston's Warrant
scenes.description: Lyle Preston makes his offer: give him the ledger and the negatives, and nobody in the party, or anyone they name, will receive a subpoena. He promises to see the councilmen dealt with. He will in fact use the ledger to make Castellane give him thirty names, not fifteen, and the councilmen will never be charged, because Haig's friends in Washington are Preston's friends too. If refused, he gets a federal warrant for 'documents relevant to the committee's inquiry' and brings it, with two Federal Agents, to the premiere.
scenes.readAloud: 'I don't think you understand what I'm offering,' Preston says gently. 'In three weeks a great many people in this town are going to discover that they knew someone in 1938. You can be on the right side of that, or on the other one. I can make sure that your names, and the names of anyone you care about, simply never come up. All I want in return is a green book that belongs, frankly, to the government.' He takes the cap off his fountain pen. 'Shall we say Friday?'

skillChecks.success: Preston will not prosecute anyone with the ledger. He will use it as a leash on Castellane, and the councilmen, who will be useful to him, will be quietly forgiven. His promise to keep your names out is true; he keeps those promises, because it makes the next person believe him.
skillChecks.failure: Preston sounds like a man who could make all of this go away. He could. That is not the same as making it right.

encounters: Haig's lawyer, Mr. Mortimer Gaines, with a $40,000 cheque and a remark about how dangerous the boulevard is on premiere nights
The Cordova's house detective (Rival Private Eye) if the party is careless in the hotel
Clete Varney (Mob Torpedo) and two Hired Guns, if Heat is 6 or more: an attempt to take the ledger by force on Friday night, at the party's hideout

acts.title: Act 2: Arrivals
acts.description: Saturday 4 October, 6:30 to 8:40 p.m. The premiere. Limousines on Hollywood Boulevard, five thousand fans behind the ropes, flashbulbs, the radio. Vivian arrives at 8:15 in the studio's car (Bunny driving, if the party arranges it). Everyone the party has met in the campaign is here, and three groups want to stop Vivian before 8:40: Dolan's men, to arrest her; Preston's agents, to take the ledger; and Thorne, on the roof, waiting for the cue. Run it as a clock with the party split between the forecourt, the lobby and the roof.
objectives: Get Vivian down the red carpet to the microphone (or keep her away from it, if that is the plan)
Stop Dolan's arrest without a riot
Keep the ledger out of Preston's hands, or give it to him
Get to the marquee roof and find spotlight No. 2 before 8:40

scenes.name: The Forecourt
scenes.description: The red carpet, the bleachers, the radio, the parade of names. The party sees everyone: Castellane with his bankers, Haig with Councilmen Hollister and Fenwick, Preston at the edge of the light, Dolan in dress uniform with a megaphone, Shay (if free) a step behind Castellane, Helen Mabry and Amy Okada (if the party invited them) in the bleachers, Mags Fennimore in a 1919 gown on the arm of Cotton Ridley.
scenes.readAloud: Hollywood Boulevard has been turned into daylight. Six searchlights stand up from the lot across the street, white pillars a mile high that cross and recross over your head, and the marquee of the Pantheon blazes with eleven thousand bulbs: THE GILDED HOUR - WORLD PREMIERE - VIVIAN LARK. The noise from the bleachers is a solid thing. Every few seconds a limousine stops at the kerb and someone gets out and the flashbulbs go off all together like a sheet of lightning and five thousand people scream a name. At the microphone by the fountain a man in a white dinner jacket with a voice like warm syrup is saying, 'And here, ladies and gentlemen, right here in front of me, is the man who is building the San Fernando Valley, Mr. Wendell Haig!'

skillChecks.success: Dolan has two men in plain clothes at the kerb where Vivian's car will stop, with a folded paper that is a warrant. And at the edge of the light, by the lobby doors, Preston's two federal men.
skillChecks.failure: You see Dolan with his megaphone and nothing else.

skillChecks.success: You work the forecourt like a guest. Chick Lorimer, the announcer, can be persuaded to call Vivian earlier or later than the cue sheet says, which throws Thorne's timing (and gives the party a choice about when the shot comes).
skillChecks.failure: Lorimer is too busy to talk to anyone not famous.

scenes.name: The Arrest
scenes.description: Vivian's car stops at 8:15. Dolan's men step forward with the warrant ('theft of property of Club Sirocco'). Arrest in front of five thousand people and forty photographers is a terrible idea for Dolan, and the party can make him see it (Intimidation or Persuasion DC 14, or Eddie Navarro, or Ness's statement in an envelope, or P2a in Dolan's ear) or physically get Vivian past. A fight on the red carpet is +3 Heat and every newspaper's front page.
scenes.readAloud: The studio car stops at the kerb. The door opens. A silver shoe, a silver gown, and Vivian Lark steps out into the light, and the bleachers rise with a sound like surf, and in the same moment two men in brown suits step out of the crowd at the rope with a folded paper, and one of them says, quite politely, 'Miss Lark? Dorothy Pell? Police. You'll want to come with us.'

skillChecks.success: Dolan, shown what the party has on him, waves his men off and becomes very busy with his megaphone. He will try to leave town on Monday.
skillChecks.failure: Dolan's men take Vivian's arm. You have one round to do something about it before she is in a radio car.

scenes.name: The Ladder
scenes.description: Whoever goes for the roof: up the stairs to the projection booth corridor, the iron ladder, the hatch, and out into the klieg lights. Thorne is at No. 2 spot with three other operators who know nothing, and his Getaway Driver is in the alley. Time it against the cue.
scenes.readAloud: The projection corridor is hot and dark and roaring with the noise of the projectors running the newsreel inside, and the iron ladder at its end goes up into a square of white light so bright it looks solid. You climb into it. The roof is a furnace. Klieg lights in a row along the parapet, each the size of an oil drum, humming and spitting, their beams pouring down onto the forecourt so that the street below is a lake of light with tiny people in it. You cannot see the operators' faces; you can see shapes against the glare, and one shape at the second spotlight has taken off his hat at last, and is kneeling.

skillChecks.success: You reach Thorne's position before he knows anyone is on the roof. Surprise.
skillChecks.failure: Thorne hears the hatch. He does not stop; he simply decides to take care of the party first, coldly, and then the cue.

skillChecks.success: Through the glare: the rifle across the spotlight's housing, and the man. You have him.
skillChecks.failure: You are blinded by a klieg light as you come out of the hatch (Constitution save DC 13 or blinded until the end of your next turn).

encounters: Emory Thorne (The Professional) at No. 2 spot, with a hunting rifle and a .45 automatic; three innocent lamp operators who get in the way; a Getaway Driver in the alley
Lt. Dolan (Bent Detective) and two Crooked Cops with a warrant at the kerb
Lyle Preston and two Federal Agents with a federal warrant at the lobby doors
If Ambler is dead: Tiny Bascombe in the crowd, looking for Thorne, who killed his boss; he is a wild card who will help anyone going after Thorne
Twelve Beat Cops on crowd duty, who will react to gunfire in about a round

acts.title: Act 3: What Goes Into the Microphone
acts.description: 8:40 p.m. Chick Lorimer calls Vivian Lark to the microphone. Spotlight No. 2 swings onto her. Whatever happened on the roof has happened. Now there is a woman in a silver gown in a circle of light with a radio audience of a million and the ledger in her bag, and the party, who have been everywhere in this city in twelve days, decides with her what she says. Then the epilogue.
objectives: Decide what becomes of Harlan Shay

scenes.name: Twenty Seconds
scenes.description: The cue. If Thorne is stopped, the light holds on Vivian and she speaks. If he is not stopped, he fires on the twentieth second, and the GM should have Harlan Shay, if he is on the forecourt and free, step into the light in front of her (Shay takes the shot; he dies or is badly hurt, the party's choice when they reach him). If Shay is not there, Vivian is hit (she drops to 0 hit points and makes death saves; Dr. Pryor or any Doctor can save her). No other outcome kills her outright.
scenes.readAloud: 'Ladies and gentlemen,' says Chick Lorimer into the microphone, and his voice booms off the front of every building on the boulevard, 'the star of The Gilded Hour, home at last, Miss Vivian Lark!' And a circle of white light lands on her by the fountain, so bright that her gown seems to be on fire, and the crowd's roar goes up and up, and she steps up to the microphone with her evening bag in both hands, and opens it.

skillChecks.success: Vivian looks for one of you before she speaks. She wants to know. Whatever you signal, she will see it.
skillChecks.failure: She does not look for anyone. She has decided.

scenes.name: The Choice
scenes.description: The GM lays out, through what the characters know, what each road costs. Vivian prefers road 1 under her own name. The party can support her, persuade her (Persuasion DC 15, or less if they have a better plan), or stop her. Roads: (1) THE TRUTH, LIVE: she reads the ledger into the microphone, or hands it to Roz Keane and the Courier, which cannot spike a story that has gone out on the radio. Haig is indicted, Hollister and Fenwick resign, the vote dies, Castellane Pictures goes into receivership, six hundred people lose their jobs, Vivian's career ends with her photograph beside a councilman on every front page, and Preston calls the studio a nest of subversives and names Kurland anyway, unless Castellane was persuaded to tear up his list. (2) THE COMMITTEE: the ledger goes to Preston. The party is safe and owed by Washington; the vote passes; Castellane gives thirty names; nobody is charged. (3) THE MONEY: sell it to Castellane for $25,000 or Haig for $40,000; nothing changes; Thorne, if alive, is paid to forget the party. (4) THE LEVER: keep it, and use it quietly: Castellane refuses the committee and leaves the syndicate, Hollister and Fenwick vote no, Haig deeds the Okada grove back to the family. Nobody goes to prison, Mabry and Kurland stay accidents, and the party holds a gun to the city's head for the rest of their lives (permanent Heat 3). Mixed roads are possible and should be allowed: the Okada deed and the councilmen's resignations as the price of silence, the DA rather than the radio, Shay's testimony rather than the ledger.
scenes.readAloud: In the white circle Vivian Lark has the green ledger open in her gloved hands. Behind her, in the front row of the forecourt, Wendell Haig is smiling the smile of a man who does not yet understand what she is holding, and Bernard Castellane, who does, has closed his eyes. Lyle Preston has taken one step forward out of the dark. The microphone is a foot from her mouth. A million people are listening. She looks at you.

skillChecks.success: Vivian takes the party's road, if it is not hers, and does it with all her heart. She will not forget that you asked.
skillChecks.failure: Vivian takes her own road. You can stop her physically. She will never forgive you, and she will be right.

scenes.name: Harlan Shay
scenes.description: Whatever happened at the microphone, Shay is left. If he is alive: the party can take him to the District Attorney's office on Monday (with the K2 and P2 clues he will plead to manslaughter and testify against Dolan, Ness, Haig and the councilmen; he gets five years), let him go to Mexico, make him the witness that turns road 4 into something closer to justice, or let him walk to the microphone himself and confess (he will, if asked; it is the most public thing he has ever done, and it brings everything down, ledger or no ledger). If he stepped in front of Thorne's bullet, the party reaches him on the flagstones by the fountain.
scenes.readAloud: He is sitting on the edge of the fountain in his beautiful grey suit, with his bandaged hand in his lap, looking at the water, while the flashbulbs go off over the boulevard behind him. 'Twenty years,' he says, 'I have been making problems go away. It's a good trick. You'd be amazed how few problems there really are, once you know what everybody wants.' He takes off his hat and turns it round in his fingers. 'I knew what Abel wanted. That was the trouble.' He looks up. 'Well. I'm a problem now. Make me go away. I'll go wherever you say.'

skillChecks.success: He means it. He will go where he is sent. It is the only kind of penance he knows how to do: to be handled.
skillChecks.failure: You cannot tell if he is sorry or simply finished.

scenes.name: The Last Reel
scenes.description: The epilogue. Narrate what happens over the next three weeks according to the choice: the council vote on 7 October, the committee's hearings opening on 20 October, the studio's fate, Vivian's, the Okadas', Mrs. Mabry's. Give each player character a closing image. Then the last line: the searchlights over Hollywood the following Saturday, for someone else's premiere, as if nothing had happened.
scenes.readAloud: On the following Saturday night there is another premiere, on Wilshire Boulevard this time, for another studio's picture, and from wherever you are in the city you can see the searchlights going up into the dark, six white columns crossing and recrossing over the hills, slow and patient and beautiful, as if they were looking for something, as if they had been looking for it every night for years, and would go on looking, whether anyone ever found it or not.

encounters: Emory Thorne, if still loose, fleeing down the alley to his car; a Getaway Driver; a chase through Hollywood (Driving, the campaign's chase rules) that ends at the city line or in a crash
Wendell Haig, who in the last resort shouts 'Get him!' at Clete Varney and two Hired Guns in the crowd, and who must be stopped by people, not shot; he fights through other men
The crowd: five thousand fans, panicking if there are shots

npcsInvolved.name: Bernard Castellane, 64
npcsInvolved.role: Founder and head of Castellane Pictures; Haig's silent partner
npcsInvolved.description: Came from nothing with a camera, a horse and a cousin in 1921. Stooped, sharp, sentimental, ruthless, an unlit cigar. Loves his studio more than any person in it, and believes he loves the people too.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Keep the studio open. He will pay anything, including other people's names. He can be shamed into courage once, if the party finds the way.

npcsInvolved.name: Wendell Haig, 58
npcsInvolved.description: Booming, pink, beloved by veterans' groups, a blue-stoned ring. At the premiere in the front row with two councilmen. Never fires a gun; points.
npcsInvolved.motivation: The vote on Tuesday. He thinks the premiere is a party.

npcsInvolved.name: Emory Thorne, 45
npcsInvolved.description: Grey suit, grey hat, forgettable face. On the Pantheon roof as spotlight operator No. 2. Patient, efficient, never angry, and leaves the moment a job goes wrong.
npcsInvolved.motivation: The fee. If the job fails, he is gone by Sunday and never comes back to California.

npcsInvolved.name: Harlan Shay, 52
npcsInvolved.role: The client; the man at the pool
npcsInvolved.description: Finished, and knows it. Asks the party what to do with him.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To be handled. If given the chance to do one brave thing, he will.

npcsInvolved.name: Lyle Preston, 38
npcsInvolved.description: At the edge of the light with a warrant and two federal agents. He keeps his promises, which is what makes him dangerous.
npcsInvolved.motivation: The ledger as a leash on Castellane; names for the hearings.

npcsInvolved.name: Lt. Frank Dolan, 55
npcsInvolved.description: Dress uniform, megaphone, a warrant in his pocket for Vivian's arrest.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Keep his pension and his lake cabin. Breaks when shown P2a.

npcsInvolved.name: Chick Lorimer
npcsInvolved.role: KHLW radio announcer at the microphone
npcsInvolved.description: Voice like warm syrup, white dinner jacket, has announced four hundred premieres and never once heard what anyone said.
npcsInvolved.motivation: A smooth broadcast. He will not cut a live microphone on a star; it would be the end of him.

npcsInvolved.name: Vivian Lark, 24
npcsInvolved.role: The star of The Gilded Hour; companion
npcsInvolved.description: In a silver gown, with a green ledger in her evening bag.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To say it out loud, under her own name. She will listen to the party. She will decide.

rewards.money: Depends entirely on the choice: nothing for the truth; Preston's goodwill for the committee; $25,000 or $40,000 for the money; nothing and everything for the lever. Shay's last $5,000 in cash, if he goes to the DA, he gives to the party 'for Abel's funeral and Mrs. Sloane's teacup and whatever else you think'.
items: Emory Thorne's hunting rifle and Rifle rounds (5), if taken; his .45 automatic and .45 rounds (14)
The green ledger and the negatives, unless given away
The Okada grove's deed, if Haig is made to sign it over
A print of The Gilded Hour, from Agnes Whitlow, 'for whatever's left of the evening'
The city's attention, for better or worse

twists: There is no right answer at the microphone. The truth costs six hundred jobs and Vivian's career and feeds the committee; silence costs justice for two dead men; the money costs nothing but the party's souls; the lever makes the party the new fixers of Los Angeles. Let the players feel all of it.
Harlan Shay, the client and the killer, may die saving the woman he sent to the Sirocco. If he does, it does not redeem him and it is not nothing.
Bernard Castellane can be shamed into refusing the committee. It is the one act of courage available to anyone powerful in the campaign, and it only happens if the party gets him there.
Lyle Preston is the only person in the story who never breaks a promise, and he is the most dangerous person in it.
The klieg lights that make Vivian a star are the cover for the man sent to kill her. The title is the trap.
dmTips: Act 1 is a sequence of conversations with powerful people. Let each make their case well. The players should leave Castellane's office with genuine doubt about whether the truth is worth six hundred jobs, and leave Preston's suite more frightened than they have been all campaign.

Thorne's plan has three clues and the party should find it. If they do not, give Shay the line about Haig placing 'Thomas' on the searchlight crew, and if they still miss it, let Tiny Bascombe, who is hunting Thorne for killing Ambler, tell them where Thorne will be. The rooftop fight should happen.
Run Act 2 as a clock: 8:15 Vivian's car; 8:20 Dolan's arrest; 8:30 Preston moves on the ledger; 8:40 the cue. Split the party. Cut between the forecourt and the roof at the tensest moments.

The rooftop fight is a set piece: the klieg lights are hazards (blinding, 2d6 fire if shoved into one, exploding if shot), the parapet is a two-storey drop onto the marquee and another onto the crowd, the three innocent operators must not be hurt, and Thorne will try to finish his shot even while fighting. He leaves by the ladder the moment he is at half hit points.

At the microphone, slow down. Describe the faces. Let the players talk among themselves in character. If Vivian is a companion played by the GM, give her one last speech about why she wants to say it. Then let the players decide and do not punish whatever they choose: give each road its true consequences and its true small graces.

Mixed outcomes are good outcomes. The party might give the DA Shay's testimony and the ledger, keep the negatives of Vivian out of the papers, make Haig sign the Okada deed, and let Preston go hungry. Reward cleverness that finds a road with fewer casualties; do not invent a perfect one.
Level-up note: the 7500 XP in this file is per character and takes each character from 5th to 6th level, the campaign's cap. Award it at the epilogue.

Period texture: searchlights like temple columns, klieg lights humming on the marquee, a radio announcer's syrup, flashbulbs in volleys, mink and silver lamé, the newsreel before the picture, a newsboy on Monday shouting the result of the council vote, and on 20 October, on every radio in Los Angeles, the committee's hearings beginning in Washington.
